source.title: GTM: A General Time-series Model for Enhanced Representation Learning of Time-Series data
source.authors: Cheng He; Xu Huang; Gangwei Jiang; Zhao-Yi Li; De-Fu Lian; Hong Xie; En-Hong Chen; Xi-Jie Liang; Zengrong Zheng; Patrick P. C. Lee

record.file_problem: The full paper text and appendices are present. The header identifies it as published at ICLR 2026, despite the supplied venue field saying ICLR.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates scaling in a new modality, time-series forecasting, and reports downstream error as pre-training data and model size vary. It does not reproduce the original language-model cross-entropy measurement or fit power laws.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the GTM model-size sweep in Figure 5 and the pre-training-data-size sweep in Table 27. Other downstream benchmark results and scaling statements cited from Kaplan et al. are not results about the scaling sweep and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study pre-trains a time-series foundation model (GTM) on 1G, 2G, 4G and 12G of UTSD data and at several depths (3–12 layers) and widths (256–768). It reports downstream fine-tuned forecasting MSE (Table 27, Figures 5–6). This gives qualitative evidence on V5 (scaling beyond text) in a new modality. It fits no power law, reports no exponents and no held-out pre-training loss, and the data range spans only about one order of magnitude.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim GTM 'follows scaling laws': forecasting MSE improves with deeper and wider models and with larger pre-training data, though width may not help at insufficient depth. They make this claim without fitting any power law or measuring pre-training loss.
record.recipe_differences: This is a time-series model evaluated with downstream forecasting MSE, not a language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling-law fit. It reports qualitative trends rather than fitted power laws or exponents.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with forecast horizon: several individual horizon results are flat or non-monotonic across data sizes. The text also says width may not improve performance at insufficient depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream fine-tuned forecasting MSE of a time-series foundation model improves modestly and monotonically with pre-training data size, mostly at long horizons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream task performance of non-language foundation models improves with pre-training scale, more at harder (longer-horizon) tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026), as stated in the text
record.problems: The scaling evidence is limited to one model family and downstream forecasting MSE. The study does not fit power laws or report exponents, and Table 27 reports no uncertainty for the data-size sweep. Its stated generalization is qualified by model width sometimes not helping at insufficient depth.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported scaling-sweep outcomes were left out. Rows use Table 27 values for MSE at each stated forecast length and the reported averages; Figure 5 values are recorded as figure-only because the text does not give their numbers.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small fitted runs.
No fixed-parameter-count shape comparison; depth and width vary total size.

Power-law functional form, exponents and pre-training loss are not tested. The data range is only 1G–12G (about one order of magnitude). Other modalities, repeated data and transfer laws are not tested.
No language-model downstream results. The time-series downstream trend is recorded under V5 and fits_no_version.

missing.what: Numeric MSE values and parameter counts for each depth×width configuration in the model-size sweep (y-axis spans roughly 0.40–0.44).
MAE columns for the data-size sweep are not recorded as rows.

record.verdict_notes: V6 links were removed from all rows. V6 concerns language-model downstream predictability, while this is a time-series model, so the downstream trend is placed under V5 and fits_no_version. The 1G rows are baseline cells, not effects. Several 'reversed'/'observed' states on changes of ±0.001 are reset to absent. The model-size sweep confounds depth and width with total size and gives no parameter counts. Table 27 reports no uncertainty, although Table 19 CIs for the 12G model are about ±0.001–0.003, comparable to many of the sweep differences.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model cross-entropy loss is measured as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No power law fitted on small runs is used to predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between model parameters and training tokens is evaluated.
The study does not compare depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.

The study evaluates qualitative scaling in time-series forecasting, but does not fit or test a power-law form, estimate exponents, or measure held-out pre-training loss. It tests one time-series model family and does not evaluate image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning scaling laws, or transfer scaling laws.
The study reports downstream forecasting MSE versus pre-training data size and model size, but does not fit a predictive curve or relate downstream performance to pre-training loss.
No comparison of fitting choices, parameter-counting conventions, or alternative scaling-law fits is reported.

relationships.condition: GTM pre-training data sweep 1G–12G, ETTh1 all horizons and Weather 336/avg, downstream fine-tuned MSE
relationships.reason: MSE falls monotonically but only 2–6% over 12x data, with no power-law fit (scale_ett_avg_12g, scale_weather_avg_12g, scale_ett_96_12g, scale_weather_336_12g).
relationships.display_finding: MSE decreased monotonically by only 2–6% with twelve times the pretraining data.

relationships.condition: Weather short horizons (96, 192) and ETTh1 192 at 2G
relationships.reason: MSE stays flat (0.147, 0.193→0.192) as data grows 12x, so no data-scaling gain appears (scale_weather_96_12g, scale_weather_192_12g, scale_ett_192_2g).
relationships.display_finding: MSE remained at 0.147 or changed only from 0.193 to 0.192 despite twelvefold data growth, with another flat result at 2G.

relationships.reason: MSE drops clearly from 0.364 to 0.310 as data grows 1G→12G (scale_weather_720_4g, scale_weather_720_12g); direction only, no fitted form.
relationships.display_finding: MSE decreased from 0.364 to 0.310 as data increased from 1G to 12G, without a fitted scaling form.

relationships.condition: GTM model-size sweep on ETTh1 (layers 3–12, dims 256–768)
relationships.reason: Text says deeper and wider models improve MSE, but width may not help at shallow depth; figure-only, no counts (scale_model_depth, scale_model_width_caveat).
relationships.display_finding: Deeper and wider models improved MSE, but additional width could fail to help shallow models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GTM time-series forecasting, pre-training data-size sweep
reader_labels.reason: MSE generally improves with more pre-training data, but the study does not fit or establish a power-law form; the displayed horizon-level results also include flat or reversed changes. Rows scale_ett_96_1g through scale_weather_avg_12g.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Average forecasting MSE across prediction lengths on ETTh1 and Weather as pre-training data increases from 1G to 12G
reader_labels.reason: The reported average MSE decreases across the tested data sizes for both datasets. Rows scale_ett_avg_1g through scale_weather_avg_12g.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Individual forecast horizons and model-width changes
reader_labels.reason: Some horizon-specific MSE values are unchanged or worsen as data increases, and width may not help when depth is insufficient. Rows scale_ett_192_2g, scale_weather_96_2g, scale_weather_96_4g, scale_weather_96_12g, scale_weather_192_4g, scale_model_width_caveat.
